async def act(page):
    import asyncio

    # Add the 'Brown' option to the global color attribute so it becomes available for products.
    # None of the knowledge_base helper functions are available, so we won't call any.

    # 1) Go to Manage Attributes (use a relative goto)
    await page.goto('/index.php/admin/catalog/product_attribute/index/')
    await page.wait_for_load_state('networkidle')
    await asyncio.sleep(1)

    # 2) Find the attribute link for "color" by scanning links and following its href with page.goto
    color_link = None
    links = page.get_by_role('link')
    total_links = await links.count()
    for i in range(total_links):
        l = links.nth(i)
        try:
            text = (await l.inner_text() or "").strip()
        except Exception:
            text = ""
        if 'color' in text.lower():
            color_link = l
            break

    if color_link is None:
        raise Exception('Could not find a link to the color attribute on the Manage Attributes page')

    href = await color_link.get_attribute('href')
    if not href:
        raise Exception('Found color link but it has no href')

    # Navigate to the attribute edit page via its href (use goto instead of click to allow further selectors)
    await page.goto(href)
    await page.wait_for_load_state('networkidle')
    await asyncio.sleep(1)

    # 3) Locate the form or group that contains the options controls
    form = page.get_by_role('form')
    if await form.count() == 0:
        form = page.get_by_role('group')

    # 4) Try to click an "Add Option" control inside the form if present
    add_clicked = False
    add_candidates = ['Add Option', 'Add New', 'Add New Row', 'Add New Option']
    for name in add_candidates:
        try:
            btn = form.get_by_role('button', name=name)
            if await btn.count() > 0:
                await btn.first.click()
                add_clicked = True
                break
        except Exception:
            pass

    if not add_clicked:
        for name in add_candidates:
            try:
                lnk = form.get_by_role('link', name=name)
                if await lnk.count() > 0:
                    await lnk.first.click()
                    add_clicked = True
                    break
            except Exception:
                pass

    # It is possible the UI already exposed an empty option row; give the UI a moment to render
    await asyncio.sleep(0.8)

    # 5) Fill the last textbox inside the form with 'Brown'
    textboxes = form.get_by_role('textbox')
    tb_count = await textboxes.count()
    if tb_count == 0:
        page_textboxes = page.get_by_role('textbox')
        page_tb_count = await page_textboxes.count()
        if page_tb_count == 0:
            raise Exception('No textboxes found to enter the new option label')
        await page_textboxes.nth(page_tb_count - 1).fill('Brown')
    else:
        await textboxes.nth(tb_count - 1).fill('Brown')

    await asyncio.sleep(0.5)

    # 6) Click Save (this click likely navigates away; per guidance make navigation-causing click the last action)
    save_candidates = ['Save Attribute', 'Save Attribute(s)', 'Save']
    saved = False
    # Prefer Save button inside form
    for name in save_candidates:
        try:
            btn = form.get_by_role('button', name=name)
            if await btn.count() > 0:
                await btn.first.click()
                saved = True
                return
        except Exception:
            pass

    # Fallback to Save button at page level; clicking it will be the last action
    for name in save_candidates:
        try:
            btn = page.get_by_role('button', name=name)
            if await btn.count() > 0:
                await btn.first.click()
                saved = True
                return
        except Exception:
            pass

    if not saved:
        raise Exception('Could not find a Save button to persist the new option')

Step 2: I need to open the color attribute for editing. There are no knowledge_base helper functions available, so I will scan the page.get_by_role('link') elements looking for one whose visible text contains 'color' (case-insensitive). Once found, I'll read its href and use page.goto(href) to navigate to the attribute edit page. I prefer page.goto over clicking the link because guidance warns about clicking links that navigate and then trying to use selectors after navigation. Using goto lets me continue interacting reliably.

Step 3: On the attribute edit page, I'll locate the main form via page.get_by_role('form'), falling back to a group role if no form role exists. This is where option controls are usually placed.

Step 4: I'll attempt to click an "Add Option"-type control inside that form (candidate names: 'Add Option', 'Add New', 'Add New Row', 'Add New Option') using form.get_by_role(). If not found, I'll also try link variants. This follows the requirement to scope button/link clicks to their parent element (form.get_by_role(...)).

Step 5: After ensuring an option row exists, I'll fill the last textbox inside the form with 'Brown' (or the last textbox on the page as a last resort). I use form.get_by_role('textbox') and fill the last one.

Step 6: Finally, I'll save the attribute. Because a Save click likely navigates away, I'll make that the last action. I first try a Save button inside the form (scoped search), then fall back to a page-level Save button. If found, I click it and return.
